question: A conference organiser wants Claude to help plan the run-up to a 400-delegate event. Which input will make the resulting plan most useful?
options: A) The actual dates, the team's availability and the tasks that went wrong last year
B) The delegate list and the venue's promotional brochure for this year's conference
C) A request to produce the most thorough conference plan that Claude is able to write
D) A note that the event is important and that the plan must not miss anything at all
correct_answers: A) The actual dates, the team's availability and the tasks that went wrong last year
explanations: Correct. Real dates, real capacity and the known failure points from last year are the material that makes a plan specific to this event rather than a template anyone could have written.
A delegate list and a brochure describe who attends and how the venue markets itself, neither of which shapes the run-up schedule.
Asking for thoroughness without supplying facts produces length, not fit; the plan still has to guess the constraints.
Emphasis is not information. Telling Claude the event matters gives it nothing new to plan around.
